articles.title: Newhey mother receives hundreds of birthday cards after son’s appeal
articles.excerpt: Wendy Bamford, 79, celebrated her birthday at Springhill Hospice, receiving an outpouring of cards and gifts following her son's heartfelt request on social media.
articles.content_html:
Wendy Bamford, 79, of Newhey, celebrated her birthday at Springhill Hospice, receiving hundreds of cards after her son Stephen appealed for messages on Facebook.

Stephen Bamford, 42, who runs Cryers Butchers in Littleborough, posted his request on 30 October, asking people to send cards to his mother, who is undergoing treatment for renal cancer.

Wendy expressed a desire for cards to read on her birthday, which fell on 4 November.

The appeal garnered significant attention, with over 1,000 likes and more than 200 comments and shares. Wendy received not only cards but also flowers, chocolates, and even spending money, with messages coming from as far away as Spain and Australia.

A local teacher and two schoolchildren also visited to deliver handmade pictures for her.

Wendy expressed her gratitude, stating, "It makes me feel cared and wanted. It’s just been overwhelming." Stephen thanked everyone who responded, saying, "You have restored my faith in humanity. Every card, every gift and every kind word means so much."

articles.title: Rochdale Masters and Mayfield Movers raise nearly £15,000 in charity walks
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale Masters Rugby League and Mayfield Movers have raised £14,698.67 for charity through two fundraising walks, with proceeds supporting community rugby and health initiatives.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Masters Rugby League and Mayfield Movers raised £14,698.67 for charity through two fundraising walks, with the latest event taking place on 31 October 2026, starting from Ince Rose Bridge ARLFC.

The walk covered a distance of 44 miles, taking more than 15 hours to complete and passing through 10 community rugby league clubs across Greater Manchester. Participants raised £6,141.80 during this latest walk, contributing to the overall total.

The Motor Neurone Disease Association will receive at least £1,500 from the fundraising efforts, while the three charities involved will receive a combined minimum of £4,500.

The Rochdale Masters will cover all fundraising transaction fees, ensuring that the remaining proceeds support the Rochdale Masters section and community activities.

In October 2025, the groups raised £8,556.87, demonstrating their ongoing commitment to improving physical and mental wellbeing in the community.

evidence_sources.captured_text: Rochdale Masters and Mayfield Movers raise almost £15,000 in two walks | Roch Valley Radio On Air Live now — track details aren't available right now Listen Live Watch Rochdale Masters and Mayfield Movers raise almost £15,000 in two walks David Murphy News Editor November 20, 2026 | 12:22 PM Print Rochdale Masters Rugby League and Mayfield Movers have raised £14,698.67 for charities and community rugby league through two walking challenges. Their latest walk raised £6,141.80, with three charities set to receive at least £1,500 each. Walkers set off from Ince Rose Bridge ARLFC in Wigan at 6.30am on Saturday 31 October 2026 for the 44-mile All Together Walk. The route took in 10 community rugby league clubs across Greater Manchester, passing through Leigh, Salford and Bury before the group reached Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC at 9.48pm. Volunteers and supporters helped the group during the walk, which took more than 15 hours. Rugby league clubs along the route welcomed the walkers with refreshments and encouragement. The Motor Neurone Disease Association, the Rugby League Cares Brain Health Fund and Springhill Hospice in Rochdale will each receive at least £1,500. The three charities are due to receive a combined minimum of £4,500. Rochdale Masters has committed to covering all fundraising transaction fees so that each charity receives its full allocation. The remaining proceeds will go towards developing the Rochdale Masters section and helping people stay active, socially connected and involved in rugby league. The same groups raised £8,556.87 in October 2025 by walking 52 miles from Rochdale to Blackpool. Mayfield Movers is a community walking group based at Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC, where Rochdale Masters also operates. Both groups aim to help people of different ages, backgrounds and abilities take part in physical activity, build friendships and improve their physical and mental wellbeing. Carl Abraham, founder of Rochdale Masters and Mayfield Movers, said, “When we first started organising these challenges, our ambition was simple: bring people together, push ourselves beyond our comfort zones and raise as much money as possible for some truly worthwhile causes. Last year’s 52-mile walk to Blackpool was a tremendous success, raising over £8,500, and to follow that up with another £6,000-plus this year is absolutely fantastic. To think we’ve now raised £14,698.67 through just two challenges is something I’m incredibly proud of, and it’s a testament to the commitment and generosity of everyone involved. Walking 44 miles was never going to be easy, but the determination, resilience and togetherness shown throughout the day were absolutely outstanding. Knowing that three fantastic charities will each receive a minimum of £1,500 makes every single mile worthwhile. But for me, this has always been about much more than fundraising. Both Rochdale Masters and Mayfield Movers were established to bring people together, build friendships, improve physical and mental wellbeing and create opportunities for people to be part of something positive. These challenges demonstrate exactly what we’re trying to achieve and highlight the important role that grassroots sport and community activities can play in people’s lives. I couldn’t be prouder of everyone who contributed, whether they completed the full distance, walked part of the route, provided support, sponsored us or made a donation. I also want to express my sincere appreciation to the rugby league clubs who welcomed us along the way. Their hospitality, encouragement and generosity were absolutely first class and demonstrated everything that’s special about our rugby league community. We’ve established something really special through these challenges, and I genuinely hope we can continue building on this success for many years to come. Almost £15,000 raised in two years is an incredible achievement, but the friendships, togetherness and positive impact we’ve created along the way are equally important. An outstanding effort from an incredible group of people, and something everyone involved should be extremely proud of.” Add Roch Valley Radio as a preferred source on Google News to see more of our local reporting Add as a preferred source on Google Do you have a story for us? articles.title: Tributes paid to Obesi Osi-Iyere, 20, former Cardinal Langley student
articles.excerpt: Obesi Osi-Iyere, a talented playwright and former student at Cardinal Langley RC High School, has died at the age of 20.
articles.content_html:
Obesi Osi-Iyere, 20, a former student at Cardinal Langley RC High School in Middleton, has died, prompting heartfelt tributes from her school community.

Obesi passed away on 28 October 2026 and was laid to rest this week. She excelled in her A-levels, achieving two A* and two A grades in mathematics, further mathematics, English language, and economics, before beginning her studies at the University of Warwick.

In a tribute, Cardinal Langley described Obesi as an "exceptional young person who had the world at her feet." The school highlighted her talent in writing and playwriting, noting that she was shortlisted for the Mustapha Matura Award in 2023 for her work, Untitled Emotions.

Obesi completed her Sixth Form studies in August 2025 and was pursuing a BSc in mathematics, operational research, statistics, and economics at university.

The school community has expressed deep sadness over her passing, reflecting on her achievements and the impact she made during her time at Cardinal Langley.

articles.title: Schofield Street, roadworks in Heywood from 20 November 2026
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council lists work affecting Schofield Street in Heywood; expected timings: Work began at 8am on Friday, 20 November 2026 and will continue for a maximum of 21 days (11 December 2026), or until repairs are complete if sooner..
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has published a traffic notice for Schofield Street in Heywood. The council lists the expected start and finish as Work began at 8am on Friday, 20 November 2026 and will continue for a maximum of 21 days (11 December 2026), or until repairs are complete if sooner..

The council gives the reason as To resurface the road. The notice describes the affected area as follows: Part of Schofield Street has been temporarily closed.

The closure begins at the junction with Walton Street and ends 138 metres up the road in a northerly direction.

The published alternative route is Walton Street, Manchester Road, Manchester Street, Cowburn Street and Schofield Street. These are the details in the council's current published record, rather than confirmation that work has started or finished. Readers travelling through the area can check the original Rochdale Borough Council notice for any subsequent amendments.

articles.title: Morning Briefing: Friday 20 November 2026
articles.excerpt: 9 new stories in the Rochdale borough since yesterday morning.
articles.content_html:
9 new stories in the Rochdale borough since yesterday morning.

The stories

  • Greater Manchester trial targets prolific shoplifters with new programme Rochdale
    A new initiative in Greater Manchester aims to tackle prolific shoplifting through coordinated efforts from police, probation services, and local councils.
  • Rochdale AFC launches Christmas Toy Appeal for local families in need Rochdale
    Rochdale AFC is calling on fans to donate gifts for its Christmas Toy Appeal, aiming to support local children living in poverty this festive season.
  • Person dies on tracks at Todmorden station, disrupting services to Rochdale Rochdale
    A person has died on the tracks at Todmorden station, affecting train services between Rochdale and Hebden Bridge.
  • Christmas carols with Mustard Seed Church, Heywood Heywood
    Mustard Seed Church in Heywood is holding a Christmas carol morning on Sunday 20 December, starting at 9.30am, at Ian's Gate, to the rear of 193 Manchester Road.
  • St Cuthbert’s RC High School in Rochdale placed in special measures after Ofsted inspection Rochdale
    St Cuthbert’s RC High School in Rochdale has been placed in special measures following an Ofsted inspection that highlighted serious safety issues and a lack of effective leadership.
  • Winter Wood Grotto returns to Rochdale with new show themed 'The Wild' Rochdale
    The Winter Wood Grotto, a festive tradition in Rochdale, is back with a new woodland-themed show created by Cornwall’s Rogue Otherworld.
  • Rochdale Borough Council establishes Integrated Commissioning Board Rochdale
    Rochdale Borough Council has established the Integrated Commissioning Board to enhance health and social care services across the borough.
  • Rochdale AFC reduces ticket prices for FA Cup tie against Newport County Rochdale
    Rochdale AFC has announced reduced ticket prices for their FA Cup match against Newport County on 5 December at Crown Oil Arena.
  • Breakfast with Santa at Queen's Park Café, Heywood Heywood
    Queen's Park Café in Heywood is hosting Breakfast with Santa on six mornings between Saturday 12 and Wednesday 23 December, each running from 10.30am to 12pm.

Weather: Sunny 7°C in Rochdale today.

The Morning Briefing is published every day at 9am. Got a story? Tell the newsdesk.

events.excerpt: Queen's Park Café in Heywood is hosting Breakfast with Santa on six mornings between Saturday 12 and Wednesday 23 December, each running from 10.30am to 12pm. The dates are Saturday 12, Sunday 13, Saturday 19, Sunday 20, Monday 21 and Wednesday 23 December. Children's tickets cost £16 and include a children's breakfast and a drink, Christmas craft and colour
events.content_html:
Queen's Park Café in Heywood is hosting Breakfast with Santa on six mornings between Saturday 12 and Wednesday 23 December, each running from 10.30am to 12pm.

The dates are Saturday 12, Sunday 13, Saturday 19, Sunday 20, Monday 21 and Wednesday 23 December.

Children's tickets cost £16 and include a children's breakfast and a drink, Christmas craft and colouring, a Christmas present for each child, and a meet and greet with Santa. Adult tickets cost £10 for a traditional English breakfast with instant coffee or tea.

Bookings can be made by messaging the café on Facebook, calling in at the café, or messaging 07983 737871. Spaces are only secured once paid in full and booked in advance, and the café asks families to mention any allergies when booking.

events.content_html:
Mustard Seed Church in Heywood is holding a Christmas carol morning on Sunday 20 December, starting at 9.30am, at Ian's Gate, to the rear of 193 Manchester Road.
